title: Potential for Economically Disadvantaged Students in Singapore to Under-perform
what_it_is: Potential for Economically Disadvantaged Students in Singapore to Under-perform

sections.label: OECD report on disadvantaged students
sections.summary: The Minister says OECD data show lower-SES Singapore students score higher than comparable OECD peers in reading, mathematics and science.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) whether the Government is concerned that the report by the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) released in November 2017 titled "Excellence and Equity in Education" found that economically disadvantaged students in Singapore were significantly more likely to under-perform in science in school, compared to their OECD counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: It is not true that students from lower socio-economic backgrounds in Singapore are more likely to under-perform than their Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In fact, the data from the OECD report show that students from lower socio-economic status (SES) homes in Singapore have higher average Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2015 scores than their OECD peers from comparable SES backgrounds in all the three domains measured − Reading, Mathematics and Science.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The same OECD report has found that about half of our students from the bottom 25% SES in Singapore performed much better internationally than what their home circumstances would predict.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Our proportion of resilient students is substantially higher than OECD's average of about 30% in the PISA 2015 study.

sections.label: Table on disadvantaged students' under-performance
sections.summary: A table compared disadvantaged 15-year-olds across countries, stating under-performance likelihood of 2.8 times for OECD average and 4.37 times for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I think there was a table that compared the performance of socio-economically disadvantaged students at 15 years old across different countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was stated that the likelihood of such disadvantaged students to under-perform is 2.8 times for the OECD average, but Singapore is 4.37 times.

sections.label: OECD study on lower SES students
sections.summary: The OECD study found Singapore's higher performing students outperformed the OECD average by a wider margin than lower performing lower-SES students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: What the OECD study found was that in Singapore, the higher performing students outperformed the OECD average by a wider margin than the lower performing students in the lower SES homes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, our lower SES students do outperform the lower SES students in OECD countries.

sections.label: Higher SES students' outperformance margin
sections.summary: Higher SES Singapore students outperform higher SES OECD students by a larger margin, making the overall difference greater than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The higher SES students are outperforming the higher SES students in the OECD by a larger margin, and so the difference in the outperformance of all our students is greater than the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, if one chooses that as the measure of equity, which the OECD has chosen to do, then the mathematical result is as Ms Lim has demonstrated.
